problem.title: Mutually unbiased bases in dimension six

question.summary: Three mutually unbiased bases are known in dimension six. Neither a fourth basis nor an accepted proof excluding a complete set of seven is known.
question.importance: Dimension six is the smallest case where the prime-power construction fails. A solution would clarify how finite geometry controls complementary quantum measurements.
question.unresolved: Construct at least four MUBs in dimension six, or prove that a complete set of seven cannot exist.

sourceRefs.statedTitle: Construct a set of at least 4 mutually unbiased bases in dimension six or prove that there are no 7 MUBs in H_6

targetClauses.text: The formal statement of this version, as archived from the source.
targetClauses.resolutionCriteria: Construct at least four MUBs in dimension six, or prove that a complete set of seven cannot exist.

claims.title: Peer-reviewed composite-dimension review keeps the case open
claims.text: McNulty and Weigert report that dimension six still has only three known MUBs and no accepted impossibility proof.

claims.title: Claimed proof excluding seven MUBs is not accepted
claims.text: Joka's v3 preprint loses phase and projector data in its moment-map step, then uses that missing structure in an unsupported reduction argument.

claims.title: Comment identifies an error in an earlier structural lemma
claims.text: The peer-reviewed Comment invalidates support for three dependent theorems. A Reply salvages restricted statements, not the MUB existence problem.

decisions.rationale: Status assessed against the archived statement in the 2026-08-12 primary-source audit; the evidence ledger lists the results considered.

cautions.label: Recent claim
cautions.text: Do not treat arXiv:2511.03537 as a solution. Its proof gaps are substantive, and the later peer-reviewed review still lists the problem as open.

notices.label: Proof gap
notices.title: The 2025-2026 MUB claim is not accepted
notices.text: The proposed dimension-reduction proof loses phase and projector information. A later peer-reviewed review still lists dimension six as open.
